title: Who Shall Towards Thy Chosen Seat
description: Who Shall Towards Thy Chosen Seat in Tonic Solfa to RATISBON (WERNER), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: James Merrick wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 346 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"Who shall abide in thy tabernacle?" Ps. 15”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to RATISBON (WERNER); any other Sevens, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Who shall towards thy cho-sen seat Turn, O Lord, his fa-vored feet? Who shall at thine al-tar bend? Who shall Zi-on's hill as-cend? Who, great God, a wel-come guest, On thy ho-ly moun-tain rest?

lines: Who shall towards thy chosen seat
Turn, O Lord, his favored feet?
Who shall at thine altar bend?
Who, great God, a welcome guest,
He whose heart thy love has warmed,
He whose will, to thine conformed,
He whose word and thought are one;
Lifts his willing soul to thee.
He who thus, with heart unstained,
Treads the path by thee ordained,
He shall towards thy chosen seat
Turn, O Lord, his favored feet;
He thy ceaseless care shall prove,
He shall share thy constant love.

licence: Public domain: James Merrick died in 1769.
credits: Words by James Merrick (1720–1769), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to RATISBON (WERNER) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
